meaningMnemonic: See the cool wing on the bottom? See the head with the neat feather coming out of the top? This is a bird . Tweet tweet!
If you boil a village, everything will turn black . Just imagine all those roads melting and coating everything in black tar. Picture it! It looks like Pompeii. (Oof, too soon?)
This looks like a boat coming toward you in the water. See the sail billowing on top and the reflection on the water? Yep, that's a boat. The boatiest boat that ever boated.
This box is open. There could be any number of things inside, but for now all you need to know is the meaning of this radical, which is box.

You take your head and pack clay dirt around it to just above your mouth. You need the circumference of your head for your helmet maker, and sending them a clay dirt mold of your head will just do the trick. That way they'll know your head's exact circumference!

Under a cliff, you spot a cross, slightly tilted. The cross is there to mark a famous clan that once ruled the lands below the cliff. It's a pretty unique cross, so whenever you see it there under the cliff, you'll know it honors the clan who lived there.

This is an elephant — or at least, a wannabe elephant. Look closely. It's actually a family of pigs, and the mama is wearing an elephant mask on her head for some reason. See the big ears and trunk on top? She wants to be an elephant so badly that she dressed up like one.
This is a fish . Kind of a funny-looking fish, with a weird head on top, a squat scaly body, and a tail fanning out underneath it. See the fish? Yeah, you see it.

This radical already looks like a gate , right? A high gate with pillars on either side and two small gate doors, way up at the top for some reason. Worst gate ever in terms of security, but definitely still a gate.

The radicals ground and big make up this radical. There's a big guy on the ground... who is that big guy? Embarrassingly, it's your husband . Feel the shame that he got knocked down on the ground. By what? Who? How? (It doesn't matter.) Don't confuse this with 未 (jet), though. See how 未 has a little tail at the end? That's because jets and other planes have tails, while husbands don't. At least I'd sure hope yours doesn't.

A (modified) prison radical containing a person radical. What does a person experience in prison? Lack . Prison is all about lack — lack of freedom, lack of the comforts of home, lack of privacy, lack of conversation. Yep, the life of a person in prison is defined by lack.
This kinda looks like a head with an arm under it pointing up at itself. That's why this radical means oneself . One points to oneself when one wants to… indicate oneself…

This is the radical for south . See how it's pointing south? You can think of the cross on top as a compass rose, and the arrow below (that ¥-looking part) as pointing down south. It's a compass pointing nowhere but south!

This is the stamp radical — the inking kind, not the postage kind. Why? Because it looks like a stamp stick! The top parts are thicker on one side so you can get a good grip. It even looks like the letter P — which just happens to be the last letter in "stamp"!
What happens when you put a flat surface on top of a pair of legs? You get a table .

Who's in the coffin next to that child? It's his teacher . Teachers are pretty much dead around 3 p.m. every day, and it's the kids in their class who wear them down. It ain't easy being a teacher, you know.

This radical looks kind of like a temple , don't you think? With all the layers and stuff? Just picture the top part as a roof, and the drop-looking bit at the bottom as a giant temple bell, with a monk standing beside it and ringing it with a large wooden beam. You see this kinda thing every day at a temple.
This radical looks just like a top hat. That's why it's top hat !
See the wing ? It's kind of like a bat wing with webbing. Either way, it's just a wing.

Flowers that grow out of the ground of a rice paddy after you bury fins there will grow yellow . Why? Because yellow is the color of a fish's soul, so planting flowers over their fins will turn them into a nice, pretty yellow.

While riding your scooter , you take your sword and cut out an area on the ground.  You carefully cut all the side s as you go. This area's all yours now! Hints Imagine riding your scooter around in a really large area, pressing your sword into the ground as you do. Once you've finished carving out the sides of the entire area, you claim to everyone around that this is YOUR area, and they aren't allowed in.
readingMnemonic: As you look down at your area with its sword-carved side s, you suddenly realize there is a hen ( へん ) pecking at the ground in there. "Um, excuse me, hen, I believe I said this is MY area?!" You try to kick it out, but it hops over your leg. Hints Imagine doing everything you can to get this hen out of your area, but it manages to dodge and outwit you at every turn. You even slash at it with your sword and try to run it over with your scooter, but the hen can't be stopped. This is the hen's area now. You have been defeated.

meaningMnemonic: When you take your leader 's measurement s, you realize they're too short, so you attach things to them to make the measurements more impressive. Attach some heels to the shoes, then attach another head on top of theirs. There — perfect measurements thanks to these attachments. Hints Imagine guiding your leader's dainty feet into the heeled shoes, then attaching the weird head replica. Now picture yourself trying to keep a straight face as you tell them they totally look tall enough.
readingMnemonic: You have to remember the kun'yomi reading of this kanji, and the part you need to remember is つ . So, think of how you would attach something to something else. What would you need? You'd need two ( つ ) things to put together! Hints Just focus on how attaching requires two things to remember this reading.

meaningMnemonic: This tree has an umbrella , which it's holding over its head. Strange, because trees normally like water… Turns out, this tree wasn't getting showered in water, but in dollar bill s instead. Hints The sick part is that all those bills were once this tree's friends. Picture the tree sobbing uncontrollably, as pieces of its former friends fall everywhere around it. No wonder it needs that umbrella.
readingMnemonic: And the person who gave the tree an umbrella to protect it from all those bills ? Satsu ki ( さつ ), a little girl famous for… handing out umbrellas, I guess. Makes sense that Satsuki would take care of these bills then. Hints Try to remember this little girl named Satsuki, since she'll come up whenever the reading for a kanji is さつ (there's a good handful of them). Picture her in your mind, with details like her hair and clothes. Maybe even holding an umbrella or standing by a tree? You should also know she's kind of a bookworm, I guess, in terms of personality. If you can imagine her clearly now, it'll be easy to remember さつ kanji later on.

meaningMnemonic: The bird radical and the bird kanji are the same! Hints As long as you know the radical bird you know the kanji bird.
readingMnemonic: Think of a run-of-the-mill bird , whatever comes to mind for you first is fine. Then, your lovely bird swells. The shape of a face, then a hand, start stretching the bird apart until it explodes outward. Covered in blood and feathers is Mrs. Chou ( ちょう ). Hints After bursting out of this bird, she turns her head sharply in your direction. "I don't just own the streets, I own the birds too. I'm inside every bird, and I, Mrs. Chou, can burst out at any time."

meaningMnemonic: The radical black and the kanji black are exactly the same.
readingMnemonic: You're in a completely black room. There's no way out, and you can't see. The room starts to fill with liquid. It gets in your mouth. You taste it. It's Coke ( こく )! Mm, tasty Coke. Hints You need to drink all this Coke, otherwise you're going to drown. Drink this Coke and keep tasting its cold sweetness as you drink it all to survive.

meaningMnemonic: Your boat has fins and a mouth ! It's still a boat though. Hints Picture this boat. It's still a boat, but there is a big mouth on the front and it has fins that it paddles forward with.
readingMnemonic: This boat belongs to the cen taurs ( せん ). That's probably why you've never seen a boat like it before. Hints Picture this mouth and boat with a bunch of centaurs riding in it. Centaurs have a lot more parts than humans, so it makes sense that their boats have more parts (animal ones) too.

meaningMnemonic: Your heart has a slide running through it because you want to be certain that the blood is flowing in and out of it smoothly. Given how important this is, you want to be absolutely certain . Hints Implanting a slide into your heart is certain to improve your cardiovascular health.
readingMnemonic: To be certain that the heart-slide is working, the doctor who put it there hits ( ひつ ) you in the chest a few times as a test. Hints Feel the impact as the doctor hits you again and again. You're not certain that this is safe, but you do feel certain you've got a terrible doctor.

meaningMnemonic: The elephant radical and the elephant kanji are the same. But! This kanji has another meaning: phenomenon . If you were the first person to see an elephant, you'd call it that too. Hints Picture the first Japanese person to see an elephant. He stops dead in his tracks, points and screams out, "What a phenomenon!"
readingMnemonic: Elephant s are great and all, except that when they die they turn into elephant zo mbies ( ぞう ). But you never see these zombies because the shou gun ( しょう ) has a special project in place that destroys all elephant bodies when they die. Hint: The readings and meanings for this kanji match up really nicely. ぞう is always for elephant and しょう is always for phenomenon. Remember it like this, the elephant is the zombie and the shougun keeps everyone from finding out about this phenomenon. Hints Picture the shougun standing over a pit of zombie elephants. None of these are getting out on his watch, letting people believe in such crazy phenomenons.

meaningMnemonic: This kanji uses a modified jet radical. The front area of the wing is wider than the middle area of the wing. This may seem counterintuitive, but by doing this they can fit so much more jet fuel. The jet zooms off and keeps going for a long, long time, until it reaches the end of the earth. Hints Imagine the end of the earth being like how they imagined it pre-Columbus era. Just a big drop going off into space, giant waterfalls plummeting down. Your crazy jet has made it to the very end! Congratulations!
readingMnemonic: When you get to the end of the world, you land your jet and put out a few mats ( まつ ) to sit on so you can view the sights. Hints It's surprisingly dirty down here, because all the water takes the garbage this way. That's why you sit on these mats you brought.

meaningMnemonic: Your clan is where you get your name. But not your given name, your family name . That's why people have names that mean "in a rice paddy" and "near the ferry crossing." The location of your clan determined your surname ! Hope your ancestors didn't live on "Poo Lake" or something. Hints Think about your own surname in your language. Where did it come from? Were you a clan of village dwellers? Maybe you made shoes! You should look it up and find out!
readingMnemonic: Don't worry, I'll tell you where your family name came from. Your family used to herd shee p ( し ). You read that right, your family was of the sheep clan because you took care of sheep all day. Hints Imagine your ancestors, herding sheep. Thanks to them your name means "sheep people." Thanks, great-great-great-great-great-grandpappy.

meaningMnemonic: That slide is your husband 's only fault . He loves that slide, more than you, and it's the only thing you don't like about him. Hints Imagine looking out the window of your house and watching your husband slide down his slide over and over. He's not even good at it, he falls off the side halfway down most of the time. You want to complain, but he's pretty decent otherwise. This is his only fault.
readingMnemonic: You try to come up with another fault of his so you can complain, when you see a tiny shih tzu ( しつ ) trotting by. Oh no! Before you can call out, your husband has fallen off the slide and crushed the poor thing. You hear a sharp yelp and then nothing. Hints You run outside and yell, "AHA! It's your fault that shih tzu died! You and that stupid slide!"

meaningMnemonic: The radical fish and the kanji fish are exactly the same! Hints Nothing fishy about that, right?
readingMnemonic: You catch a fish . As you pull it out of the water, it starts yelling and pointing: " GO !" ( ぎょ ). "GO GYO GYO GYO!" There's a huge cruise ship coming right towards your little fishing boat. No wonder the fish was yelling GO at you. Hints Have him continue to scream "GO GYO GYO GYO!" as you try to get your engine started and attempt to flee your impending doom. The fish helps too, because he's pretty worried as well.

meaningMnemonic: Under the canopy , you use a tree for your floor . It also becomes your bed , because hey, what is a floor but the original bed? Hints You lay it down, cut it into slats, and voila! A floor! And a bed!
readingMnemonic: It's great having a floor or bed , but whenever you use it you say yucka ( ゆか ) because it just gets so dirty. That's the one flaw of using a floor as a bed. In fact, it's the dirtiest floor you've ever seen, because it's covered in yucca ( ゆか ) leaves. You're sleeping on a yucca floor. Ew! Hints You can imagine how comfortable it is to sleep on a floor of yucca leaves, but at the same time how horrible the smell must be when they start to rot.

meaningMnemonic: The lion drops a drop of saliva onto this person from above. The person is in a much worse place compared with where they were before, since they only just recently fell into this pit. Hints Picture the person, the lion is leaning over them, the drop of spit dangling from their mouth. "I-I want to go back where I came from," the person gasps, shaking.
readingMnemonic: From above there is a loud caw, and a giant ea gle ( い ) swoops down, forcing the lion to back off. The eagle grabs the person with its talons, bringing him into the air! But now he's... in the air being carried by a giant eagle, compared with where he was before, is this really better?! Hints The eagle came from the sky and technically rescued him, but compared to where he was before, it may not be a better situation. I think this person is going to be eaten either way.

meaningMnemonic: Sew thread through your top hat and to the top hats of other people you know and you'll turn into a group of top hat wearing people. You're all connected by the thread now, so everyone will assume you're a group, even if that's all you guys have going for yourselves. Hints Picture a group of people threaded together by their top hats. Don't you want to be part of a cool group like that? Your own top hat team.
readingMnemonic: Everyone in this group loves cumi n ( くみ ). You know, the spice or seed. The group take off their top hats and fill them with cumin. You're officially a group for lovers of cumin. Hints What do you do in the cumin group? You smell the cumin. Cook with it. Taste it. This group lives and breathes cumin!

meaningMnemonic: You go down a street that cuts through a rice paddy and leads to a box . When you open the box at the end of the street, you see it's full of image s. Image after image. Drawing , painting , you name it. Someone must have left this box of images here. Hints What are the images of, anyway? Well, it's better not to say out loud. Just think of the kind of image you enjoy looking at most. That's what's in the box at the end of the street. Aren't you the lucky one?
readingMnemonic: Okay, I didn't want to tell you this, but the image s are all drawing s and painting s of ga rgoyles ( が ) and cock s ( かく ). Male chickens, that is. Turns out that's what you wanted to see most. Don't worry, no one is judging you. Hints Try to see the images of the gargoyles. Winged, stony monsters. Very cool. And the roosters? Colorful little dinosaurs. What's not to like?

meaningMnemonic: This kanji is the same as the radical it comes from. Lack becomes Lack ! Hints If you know the radical you know this.
readingMnemonic: To remember けつ , we use the word "ketsup." It's the perfect blend of ketchup and catsup! You're lack ing something in your fridge. You look around, trying to find the ketsu p ( けつ ) you lack. You can't find it, because you lack it. Hints Imagine having to use regular, ordinary ketchup, or just old, boring catsup on your burger. Or even worse, an actual tomato. BLEH!

meaningMnemonic: You're flying in a jet . Even though it's one of the fastest things on earth, your child is sitting in the back asking, "Are we there yet? Are we there yet?" You have to keep responding. " Not yet ! Not yet! NOT YET!" Hints Feel the irritation of this. How irritating is this kid going to be the whole flight over? The jet is going as fast as it can!
readingMnemonic: What a selfish kid, right? Well, all he thinks about is " Me ( み ) me me me me me me me me me me." Hate kids like that. Hints Go ahead and pretend to listen to the kid asking if we're there yet. Then in your mind go "me me me me me me me" quietly.

meaningMnemonic: The thread that ties you to your clan is paper . Your papers, that is. Hints The paper itself was also made by your clan using thread woven really tightly together.
readingMnemonic: You need this specific paper to prove that you aren't a Commi ( かみ ), aka a Communist. Or that you are. It really depends on where you want to go and what decade this is. Hints Imagine a big guard coming up to you and asking to see your papers so they can see what clan you belong to. Well you're from the Commi clan, so you really hope this guard is okay with that.

meaningMnemonic: There's a scooter with your mama carrying a task she needs to get done. You see her pass through , hurrying by to get that task done. Hints Imagine your mama passing through your house on a scooter, not stopping because she needs to get her task done urgently.
readingMnemonic: As you watch your mama pass through the house, she yells, "YOU HAVE TO DO THIS TASK TOO ( つう )!" Too?! Oh no, now you have to do it too. Hurry up! Hints Why do you have to do the task too? Because there are two tasks, so the two of you have to do them.

meaningMnemonic: The mouth clan are a group of peoples . They are the people of a nation . Hints The mouth clan are distinct peoples. They do, of course, use their mouths.
readingMnemonic: The mouth clan peoples are a nation of people who use their mouths to say mean ( みん ) things to other peoples. Hints That's why they're the mouth clan. This nation of people are known for mouthing off and saying mean things. Imagine them, as a nation, saying mean things to you. How awful! All being from the same place, they're all into it too. In a way, they're not the mouth clan, they're the mean clan.

meaningMnemonic: The king 's village is the reason he's king. Without the village there would be no reason to have a king in the first place. Hints If a king has no one to rule then he has no reason to exist.
readingMnemonic: You can't have reason without re ( り ). Hints Just like you can't have a king without a village, you can't have reason without re.

meaningMnemonic: A giant cross with a mouth stands above you. "I am reason !" it says to you. It is the Cross of Reason. Hints Because it's a cross with a mouth, it thinks that it is reason in all the chaos.
readingMnemonic: The reason that this Cross of Reason exists is to combat the you ths ( ゆう ) of the world, who just bring chaos into everything. Hints "Those youths just do things for no reason! That's why I, the Cross of Reason, am here! I will knock some reason into those youths."

meaningMnemonic: The sun in the center of the sky gives off its light, which reflect s off of everything around it. Hints Look around you, everything you see is reflecting the light of the sun. Unless it's night time, then the tiny sun in the center of your lightbulb is creating the light that reflects there.
readingMnemonic: This reflect ed light is important for a corns ( えい ), in particular. Without light reflecting off everything, the sun's light would never make it down to the ground where they've fallen. They would never grow into trees. And we'd all suffocate. Hints Picture the light of the sun reflecting off a single acorn on the forest floor. So much symbolism!

meaningMnemonic: Next to the tree , a lid is put on your father . "Hello child," he says. "This is your new school ." Hints He goes on to explain that he changed your school to here because there is a tree to block the satellite's view. Also, he wears a tin foil lid on his head so they can't track him. The regular school was no good because "they were watching." So now you have this new school, taught under a tree by your father who's wearing a lid on his head.
readingMnemonic: Your new school has other students too. They are all こう いち s, though. Hints On your first day of school, imagine walking under the tree and seeing all your classmates. They're all こういち –similar to each other, but with some variation. Your father explains these こういち s escaped from a government research facility, and they come to this school to receive a better education.  "These poor こういち s need a school that will teach them more than just kanji and Japanese vocabulary."

meaningMnemonic: When rain falls on Wolverine , it turns to snow . He's so emotionally distant and cold that the rain freezes into snow as soon as it gets near him. Hints Imagine Wolverine in the pouring rain, creating a little halo of snow around him wherever he goes. It's strangely beautiful. That is one cold, traumatized dude…
readingMnemonic: You're concerned for Wolverine's mental health. Him being so emotionally cold that he turns rain to snow means you kee p ( ゆき ) asking if he's okay. But that only makes him want to be more distant. Hints Sheesh, emotionally distant people are complicated. The more you keep trying to help them, the more they reject you. Wolverine could do with a nice holiday to melt all that snow away.

meaningMnemonic: You've seen this as a radical before, and the kanji means the same thing — south ! Hints If you keep up with your radicals, your kanji studies will never go south. Haha! Go south! Get it? I said g—
readingMnemonic: Think about the south . What's down there? Mean Amy ( みなみ ) lives down there. Think of the last mean thing she did to you and imagine it while yelling out "MEAN AMYYYYY" at the sky. Hints Picture Mean Amy down in the south, saying mean things in her American southern accent: "Y'all don't come back now, ya hear?" Man, Mean Amy is so mean. And southern.

meaningMnemonic: You keep your bow private because it's made of insect s, meaning it's extremely strong . Insect bodies are really durable, so they make for super strong bows. That's why you have to keep this one private — it's simply too strong to let others get ahold of. Hints Imagine holding this bow. Feel how strong it is as you draw the string. Now look closely at the insect bodies it's made of. Thanks for your help, little guys.
readingMnemonic: You had this strong bow made especially for you in きょう と . きょうと is famous for their strong bows, so if you ever want another, you know where to go. Hints Imagine all the people who live in きょうと , using their strong arms to make strong bows out of strong insect carapaces. Could きょうと be Japan's strongest city?

meaningMnemonic: The leaf shaped like an eye only grows in winter . Every other leaf, however, will do the opposite, which is to grow in the summer . Hints Just think of the eye leaf as weird (it is weird, after all). It grows in the winter. Now, think of any normal leaves. They do the exact opposite, which is to grow in the summer.
readingMnemonic: Now it's summertime! What do you do during the summer ? You just sit around with your favorite string tying knots ( なつ ) in it over and over again. Hints Think about summer. Now think about yourself tying knots. Now think about summer again. Now think about tying knots again. Now think about your mother getting upset at you because all you do is tie knots all summer long. Go play video games like a normal kid!

meaningMnemonic: There's a lid on your mouth and mustache , covering up all your talking holes. This is because you kept saying how tall and expensive you are. Hints Imagine yourself saying how tall and expensive you are to everyone in the room. Then they use a lid to cover your mouth so you can't talk to anyone anymore. But, then your mustache starts talking, saying the same thing. That's why this lid covers both your mustache and your mouth. Now you can't say that you are tall or expensive.
readingMnemonic: "I am tall er and more expensive than you." You're saying this because there are some こう いち s in the room, and you want to make them feel inferior (you're a こういち hater). You keep comparing your height to the こういち s in the room, and you keep checking price tags. Then you tell them you're taller and more expensive than they are. Hints The こういち s finally get tired of your shenanigans, and lid up your mouth and mustache so you can't say that you're tall or expensive.

meaningMnemonic: A teacher in winter is happiest because they get to teach ! The kids can't go out and play because it's too cold. They all have to come in and stay warm as the teacher teaches! Hints Picture a teacher excitedly teaching, bundled up in the cold. Snow falling outside. Grumpy children being taught inside.
readingMnemonic: Teachers can teach the most about Japan in winter by going to きょう と . きょうと is where all the old temples and history of Japan is centered. And it's really gorgeous when it snows. Hints Imagine the teaching teacher teaching you about Japan in きょうと in winter. You've always wanted to go to きょうと !

meaningMnemonic: The sun is used in a temple to tell time . They don't have clocks or cell phones, they have sun dials and good old fashioned "looking up and seeing where the sun is right now." This also can mean o' clock , as in "five o'clock" It's used when measuring what time it is in Japanese. Hints Imagine being in a temple and realizing you don't know what time it is. Never fear! Look on up at the sun. Ah, yes. Blinding noon.
readingMnemonic: Time in a temple makes you think of Je sus ( じ ). Specifically, Jesus being able to perform time travel magic. He winks at you, goes back to the dinosaur ages, where he wrestles a T-rex. Then, he goes to WWII era and punches Hitler in the mouth. Hints Imagine him going to all kinds of different times and also make sure you're specifically imagining Jesus doing all these things. Put these two together and you'll remember the reading in no time. (Haha, get it?)

meaningMnemonic: You have two bow s but they're both covered in ice . This has made them very weak . Hints Just look at these weak, iced-over bows. If you tried to draw back their strings they'd snap into a million pieces.
readingMnemonic: You take the bows out to your car, which is stuck in a bunch of ice and snow, and try to use them as a kind of weak jack ( じゃく ). You know, to get your car unstuck. Unfortunately, your bows are too weak and brittle to use as jacks, and they just snap in half. Hints Now you're stuck with two weak broken bows and no jack. Ice is the worst.

meaningMnemonic: Use a scooter to travel the circumference of the world and it will take you a full week . Seven whole days! Hints A week in earth time is also known as a "full scoot" in scooter lingo. ;)
readingMnemonic: If you want to scoot for a week , you'll need shoe s ( しゅう ). Good shoes too, not sandals or high heels or boots. Solid, high quality shoes, so you don't fall off the scooter and hurt yourself. Hints You can't ride a scooter for a week barefoot, are you nuts?! Get some shoes!

meaningMnemonic: You look at a table and notice it is being used as a slide by insect s to launch themselves into the wind . This kanji can also mean style . To remember this, consider how styles can change quickly, just like the wind ! Hints Picture a table tilted on its side with some of its legs longer than others, a perfect slide for insects! Imagine all the different insects jumping into the wind each in their own particular style.
readingMnemonic: You wonder what's pushing these insects to jump into the wind in such a manner, and you realize that it's because they've had way too much foo d ( ふう ). Hints The insects ate all the food that was left on the table, and now they can't just fly away into the wind like they normally do. Instead, they have to try this new style by using the table as a slide to help them take off into the wind.

meaningMnemonic: What you say to oneself (yourself), you decide to write down . Whether this is in the form of a journal, diary, or blog, you feel the need to record these important thoughts in some way. Hints Just imagine writing in a diary and saying everything to write aloud to yourself in your head. "Dear me, today I learned a lot of new kanji on WaniKani. It was the best. I love the crabigator sooooo much. Love, me."
readingMnemonic: You need to protect what you write down and record for yourself with a key ( き ). These are your special thoughts and feelings, you don't want anyone else to see! Lock them away with a key! Hints Picture the key you use to keep what you write down a secret. What does it look like? How does it feel in your hands?

meaningMnemonic: The radical yellow and the kanji yellow are exactly the same!
readingMnemonic: You're in a room, surrounded completely by yellow . You can't get out. Somewhere in the room is a yellow key ( き ) but you can't find it, because everything looks the same. You crawl around trying to find this tiny thing so that you can escape. Hints The walls are coming in closer, too. Make sure you feel a bit of peril as you look for this key. The walls have a slight opening at the bottom too, so if you don't find it before the wall goes over it, the key will be lost forever, and you'll be smushed!

meaningMnemonic: The west sun is, of course, the afternoon sun . 西日 describes the sun when it's in the western part of the sky. It generally refers to the afternoon sun, but it can also mean the setting sun or the evening sun . Basically, you can use it for sun or sunlight from mid-afternoon until sunset!
readingMnemonic: This word uses kun'yomi readings for both 西 ( にし ) and 日 ( ひ ). You've seen these readings before, so if you can remember that they're kun'yomi then you're good to go! Just watch out for that rendaku that changes ひ to び .

sentences.japanese: 西日がまぶしくて、テレビが見えません。
sentences.english: The afternoon sun is so bright I can't see the TV.

sentences.japanese: 西日でカーテンがオレンジ色に光りました。
sentences.english: The setting sun made the curtains glow orange.

sentences.japanese: 西日が強くて、サンルームがサウナみたいになっています。
sentences.english: The afternoon sun is so strong that the sunroom is like a sauna.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
readingMnemonic: Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: When you think about birds, what is the most common bird you can think of? What bird do you hate the most or like eating the most? Either one will work. Now, imagine yourself going up to that bird. You did something terrible. You tore ( とり ) off its wing and started eating it (pretend it's cooked first, if that makes you less nauseous).

meaningMnemonic: This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of black ? It's also black . readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Think of black things. One very common black thing is the common crow ( くろ ). Associate those two together.

sentences.english: black rain, rain following a nuclear explosion

sentences.japanese: プロムには黒いドレスで行こうと思う。
sentences.english: I'm thinking of going to the prom in a black dress.

sentences.japanese: ペットの犬の毛が黒いので、うちには白い羊毛のセーターが有りません。
sentences.english: Since our pet dog's fur is black, we do not have any white wool sweaters.

meaningMnemonic: A black person is simply a Black person , kind of like how a 白人 is a "White person," but a different  color.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Since 人 has two on'yomi readings, here's a mnemonic to help you remember which one to use: Imagine a Black person you know well wearing coke jean s ( こくじん ). Yep, jeans made entirely from coke bottles. That's actually a thing. Look it up if you don't believe me.

sentences.japanese: トロントには、大きな黒人のコミュニティがあります。

sentences.japanese: 母は黒人で、父はアジア人です。
sentences.english: My mother is Black and my father is Asian.

meaningMnemonic: This is simply a blue sky (aka a blue sky !).
readingMnemonic: You'd think that this word would use on'yomi readings to read it, but it doesn't (shake that angry fist at the kanji gods!). Instead, it's double kun'yomi, probably because this word is really like two separate words put together, "blue" and "sky." In the previous level you unlocked these two separate words, learning their readings. That means you should be able to read this as well. One quick note is the rendaku-fication of 空 as well. It becomes ぞら .

sentences.english: to be able to see blue sky

sentences.japanese: 五月は青空の日が多いですね。

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
readingMnemonic: Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You're riding in a boat. It's great. Imagine it being the best time you've had in your life. You tell everyone: "This is fun, eh ?" ( ふね ). You're on a Canadian ship, which is why you add the "eh" in there. Say this out loud wherever you are right now while imagining the sea smell, the wind, and the excitement of boats.

sentences.japanese: こちらは四国に行く船です。
sentences.english: This is a boat going to Shikoku.

sentences.japanese: 次の船は、何時に出ますか？
sentences.english: What time is the next ship leaving?

sentences.japanese: 船の上から見る日の出はきれいです。
sentences.english: The sunrise seen from aboard the ship is beautiful.

meaningMnemonic: What's a street eye ? Some kind of newfangled surveillance system? Actually, the eye kanji ( 目 ) is often used to mark something's position in a sequence, and that's what it's doing here. When do you position streets in a sequence? When you're planning out city district s and city block s. Just imagine eyeing each of them one-by-one as you pore over a city map with your tired, bloodshot city planner eyes. The 丁目 is one of the essential units Japanese cities are divided into. It's like a block or a neighborhood, but with an irregular shape and size. In English, it's often just written as chome .
readingMnemonic: The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji, so use those and you'll be A-OK.

sentences.english: The cover of this diary was 10,000 yen.

You learned the つく reading with 作る , but かた wasn't the main reading you learned for 方 , so here's a mnemonic to help it stick: The best thing you can teach someone how to make is a cata pult ( かた ). It's just like the old saying: give a man a catapult, and he'll besiege a castle for a day; teach a man the way of making catapults, and he can besiege castles for a lifetime.

meaningMnemonic: What do a city , a town , and a village have in common? They're all municipalities . 市町村 is a formal, administrative term that refers collectively to cities and towns and villages . readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You should be alright with 市 and 町 , but you didn't learn 村 's on'yomi with the kanji. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember it: You decide to tour all your prefecture's municipalities with your son ( そん ). It'll be a great learning experience for your son to visit all the cities and towns and villages in the area and see what each of them is like. Plus, it'll be a good parent-son bonding activity.

meaningMnemonic: You correct the moon because it's a New Year . It's the beginning of a fresh year, so you gotta have the moon in the correct position. 正月 usually refers to the first few days of a new year, and it's one of the biggest holidays in Japan. Originally, it meant the entire first month of the new year, so you still might see it used that way in some contexts — especially historical ones.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Both of these kanji have a couple of on'yomi readings, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember which ones to use: At New Year , you hate your sho gun's guts ( しょうがつ ). He doesn't celebrate New Year, you see, so none of you get any time off. He even started a war last New Year and ruined everyone's holidays. No wonder you hate that shogun's guts. Note: Since 正月 used to refer to the entire first month of the new year, it uses the がつ reading of 月 — the reading used for specific month names.

meaningMnemonic: This word starts with an お to make it more polite. Then it has the kanji 兄 which you already know. Lastly, it has さん which is an honorific to elevate people and be polite. readingMnemonic: The reading for this one is pretty tricky, and I'd consider it an exception. To remember it, you have to learn the 兄 part, and everything else will fall into place. Here's a mnemonic to help you: Your (kind) older brother pushes you down on the ground. You stand up and look at your knee ( にい ), which is all bloody. "Why'd you do that to my knee!?" you ask. meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. Because of this, it can mean to end or to begin depending on the situation, as in 冬休みが明ける (winter vacation ends) or 年が明ける (the new year begins). Think of it like a new phase in your life is "dawning."

In this case, that's あ — just like in 明かり — but since 明 's kun'yomi readings can be a little irregular, here's a mnemonic to help you out: When it starts to dawn , you gaze up at the sky and exclaim " ah " ( あ )!
